prompt.context: A French soft drink company, Le Seine, is looking to diversify its holdings by investing in a new fast food chain in the US.
prompt.question: You are hired to determine whether Le Seine should pursue this path and, if so, how they should go about execution.

clarifying_info.q: Why is the company thinking of investing in the fast food industry and not another?
clarifying_info.a: The fast food industry has been experiencing sustainable growth for the last few years, and we believe that it will continue to grow.

clarifying_info.q: Why the US market and not the French market?
clarifying_info.a: The US is more attractive economically and Le Seine has been present in the country for a few years.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company know much about the fast food industry and its consumers?
clarifying_info.a: Not very much. They are not sure where to enter.

clarifying_info.q: Has the company thought about which segment to enter?
clarifying_info.a: No. But what do you think, at a high level, which segment should they enter?

framework: Understand the company's logic for entering into the fast food industry
Examine overall trends in the fast food industry and determine which segment is most promising
Assess overall demographic changes and major trends in eating habits
Determine what competencies Le Seine can provide that will help it enter and succeed
Identify high-level entry strategies the company should consider
Use Porter's 5 Forces as a starting point: competition, substitutes, new entrants, suppliers, customers

questions.prompt: Which fast food segment should Le Seine enter and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should quickly run through pros and cons of various segments (burgers, pizza, Mexican, chicken, cold cut sandwiches, prepared meals). The prepared meals segment (e.g., Boston Market) is the recommended answer because: (1) Le Seine is French and has European appeal that fits prepared meals; (2) demographic trends favor it — aging population and more dual-income families; (3) trend toward healthier eating; (4) the segment is in a growth stage with only one or two known players and lower barriers to entry compared to burgers. Candidate should note that the burger segment is dominated by McDonald's, Burger King, and Wendy's with high barriers to entry.

questions.prompt: How can Le Seine differentiate itself from competition in the prepared meals segment?
questions.guidance: Le Seine can differentiate by: offering food with a French theme priced competitively; setting up in major grocery stores as more people purchase prepared foods during grocery shopping; capitalizing on its existing distribution and marketing experience in the US.

recommendation: Le Seine should enter the US fast food market, specifically the prepared meals segment, on a large scale to achieve economies of scale needed for competitive pricing
Quickly develop strong brand equity; explore franchising as an option
Study in detail how the most successful fast food outlets operate
Consider acquiring an existing chain versus starting a brand new one
risks: Limited knowledge of the fast food industry and consumer preferences
High capital requirements to achieve scale
Brand unfamiliarity in the US fast food space
next_steps: Evaluate franchising vs. acquisition of an existing prepared-meals chain
Identify key locations — know customers in every region and prioritize convenience
Conduct detailed competitive analysis of the prepared meals segment (e.g., Boston Market)
